# pipeline.yaml keys

Every key `spec/schemas/pipeline.schema.json` allows in a pipeline file: the top-level keys first, then the keys of a step, which `source:` and every entry of `steps:` share. A dotted key sits inside the key before the dot, and an upper-case part such as `FIELD` stands for a name you choose.

The only pipeline authoring surface in v0 (SPEC.md §9, ADR-005). Validate the YAML document after decoding it to JSON. Derived from internal/pipeline.Pipeline, which decodes with KnownFields(true) — hence additionalProperties: false.

## Top-level keys

| Key | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | Pipeline name; recorded in runs.pipeline. |
| `version` | always `1` | no | Format version. Defaults to 1 when omitted; v0 understands only 1. |
| `source` | step (see Step keys) | yes | The one source step. Required. `when:` is not allowed on it. |
| `steps` | array of step (see Step keys) | no | The pipeline's steps, executed strictly in order. Deliver-role adapters are ordinary entries (ADR-031) — any number, any position; there is no top-level deliver block. |
| `group` | string | no | ADR-021: the membership terminus. Records completing the run's final step are `added` to this group (created on demand). Valid with or without deliver steps; captures completers, not sends (ADR-031). |
| `waterfall` | any | no | Reserved (SPEC.md §9). Present only so v1 can add it without a format break; any value here MUST be rejected in v0. |

## Step keys

| Key | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | no | Step id, unique within the pipeline. Defaults to 'source' / 'step-N'. |
| `use` | string | one of `use`, `group` | Adapter id, such as 'harvest/profile'. Required everywhere except a group source, which declares group: instead. |
| `group` | string | one of `use`, `group` | ADR-021: group-as-source, valid only on the source step and mutually exclusive with use:. Members are projected from the ledger; provides are open (wildcard), needs enforced per record at run time. |
| `require` | array of string | no | ADR-021: process only records currently members of EVERY listed group. Valid on any non-source step, deliver steps included. Referenced groups must exist at plan time. |
| `exclude` | array of string | no | ADR-021: skip records currently members of ANY listed group — the judgment-memory mechanism. Valid on any non-source step, deliver steps included. Referenced groups must exist at plan time. |
| `record` | string | no | ADR-021/031, deliver steps only: the group this step's successful deliveries append `touched` events to. Defaults to the pipeline name per deliver step (steps sharing the default share the scope); created on demand. |
| `suppress` | object | no | ADR-021/031, deliver steps only: skip records with a `touched` event in the group within the window; skips are receipted with reasons and the record advances past the step. Layers above the idempotency floor. |
| `suppress.group` | string | yes | — |
| `suppress.within` | string matching `^[0-9]+d$` | yes | — |
| `with` | object | no | The step's config, validated against the adapter's config_schema. Sent as OPEN.config. On a participant step (ai/*, human/*, agent/*, text/*) it MAY carry template: (ADR-057); on a human/* step render: and prompt: (ADR-049); engine: is not a key anywhere (ADR-050). |
| `with.template` | string or object | no | ADR-057, participant steps: the operator's text, a string or {file: \<path\>} (relative to the pipeline file), in the bounded Liquid dialect of SPEC.md §10 item 10. An ai/* step renders it once over config.* (the shared block; records never enter it); a text/*, human/* or agent/* step renders it per record over config.* and record.*, the latter limited to uses:/of:. The planner parses it and refuses an unknown tag or filter, a record.* reference out of scope, or a config.* key absent from with:. |
| `with.template.file` | string | yes | — |
| `with.render` | object | no | ADR-049, human/* and agent/* steps: the fields the participant is shown per record (validated as uses:, SPEC.md §7). Default: the uses: fields, or the of: value alone; a template: (ADR-057) replaces the listing. |
| `with.render.fields` | array of string | no | — |
| `with.prompt` | one of `tty`, `never` | no | On a human/* step (ADR-049): tty (default) walks the records inside `gtme run` at a terminal, never leaves every record pending for `gtme answer`; an agent/* step is always never. Never text: an ai/* step's text is template: (ADR-057), and with.prompt there is a plan error naming it. |
| `with.engine` | not allowed | no | Removed (ADR-050): the API is the only model engine and the fixture engine is selected by environment. A step carrying engine: fails `gtme plan` naming the fix; `engine: claude-code` becomes an agent/* step answered through `gtme answer`. |
| `uses` | array of string | no | ADR-004: a participant step's dynamic needs. Valid only on steps whose adapter role is filter/compose/review (the participant roles, ADR-048: ai/*, human/*, agent/*, and text/*, ADR-057). The planner MUST validate it exactly as needs.required (SPEC.md §7), and at execution time the projected fields object MUST be built from `uses` rather than from the manifest's open-ended `needs`. |
| `of` | string | no | ADR-048: the referent — the field whose value a compose or review step is about (required on a review; an edit on a compose). Validated exactly as a uses: entry (SPEC.md §7); its current value joins the record's judgment-cache input hash, and its field_values.id is recorded as the referent of everything the step writes. |
| `when` | string matching `^[A-Za-z0-9_.\-]+\.passed$` | no | Gate. v0 supports only '\<step_id\>.passed', referencing an earlier step. |
| `cache` | string matching `^[0-9]+d$` | no | Freshness-window override for this step, such as '30d'. |
| `idempotency` | string | no | Deliver steps only (ADR-031: the planner rejects it elsewhere): the field whose value keys a delivery. Defaults to the identity key (SPEC.md §8); REQUIRED on http/deliver (ADR-023). |
| `variables` | map of string | no | Deliver steps only (ADR-018/019/031): egress mapping of target merge-field name → canonical or namespaced ledger field. Its values are the step's dynamic needs (SPEC.md §6, §7); the planner validates each against upstream provides and rejects the key on any other step. |
| `redeliver` | one of `always`, `on_change`, `never` | no | ADR-045, deliver steps only: repeat policy. Defaults to on_change when the adapter declares idempotency: native, never otherwise; always/on_change are plan errors on a target without native idempotency. |
| `on_missing` | one of `run`, `skip`, `fail` | no | Per-record completeness policy. Deliver steps (ADR-019/031, SPEC.md §8): skip (default) or fail when a variables: target does not resolve to a non-empty value — skip records a verdict and the record advances past the step; fail freezes it; blank merge fields never send, so run is not valid here. Participant steps (ai/*, human/*, agent/*; ADR-053, SPEC.md §7): run (default) dispatches the record with a declared uses: field absent and the receipt counts it; skip advances the record untouched without dispatching; fail fails it naming the missing fields. |
| `waterfall` | any | no | Reserved (SPEC.md §9); rejected in v0. |
| `provides` | array of string or object | no | ADR-033: declared output fields, valid only on participant steps (ai/*, human/*, agent/*; ADR-048). A review MUST declare its labels here. A list of field names, or an object whose keys are field names and whose values are null or declare type, enum, canonical. Bare names land as \<pipeline\>.\<name\>; a dotted name is kept as written; canonical: true lands the field on the canonical field of that name (SPEC.md §7). |
| `provides.FIELD` | null or object | no | — |
| `provides.FIELD.type` | one of `string`, `integer`, `number`, `boolean`, `array` | no | — |
| `provides.FIELD.enum` | array of string | no | — |
| `provides.FIELD.canonical` | boolean | no | SPEC.md §7: the declared name IS a canonical field of the pipeline's entity type; the output lands there, global rather than per-campaign. |
| `limit` | integer | no | ADR-032: on a group source, at most N current members, oldest-added first. ADR-054: on a traverse step, the engine-owned cap on children per parent, as on a source binding. Valid nowhere else. |
| `once` | boolean | no | ADR-052: group source only — select only members this pipeline has not already finished (completed the final step, or stopped by a filter verdict); failed and pending records stay eligible. Oldest-added first within limit. Never mutates the group; a dry or simulated run finishes nothing. |
| `respend` | boolean | no | ADR-038: declares that re-running the pipeline MAY pay for this step's records again — silences the plan's respend warning (SPEC.md §7). Not valid on the source. |

## Example

From `examples/hello.yaml`, without its header comment: a source and 3 steps, `score`, `keep`, and `out`.

```yaml
name: hello
version: 1

source:
  use: csv/source
  with:
    path: contacts.csv          # three fictional people, beside this file
    columns: { full_name: Full Name, email: Email, title: Title, company_domain: Company Website }

steps:
  - id: score
    use: demo/enrich            # $0.01 per record, pretend; cached for 30 days
    with:
      cost_per_record_usd: 0.01

  - id: keep                    # deterministic judgment in SQL: no model, no spend
    use: sql/filter
    with:
      query: >
        SELECT identity_id FROM current_values
        WHERE field = 'demo.score' AND CAST(value AS INTEGER) >= 70

  - id: out
    use: csv/deliver
    with:
      path: out.csv
    variables:
      score: demo.score
      note: demo.note
    idempotency: email          # re-runs append nothing twice
```
